clue.text: Little old star, no posh god

parts.note: O is the short form of old, a little bit of the word

indicators.note: no tells us the posh letter is taken away from the star's name

parts.note: Sirius is the Dog Star, the brightest in the night sky
U is the old label for upper-class, posh usage

explanation.surface: A minor old celebrity, lacking class, is set against a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: U for posh comes from the British 'U and non-U' distinction between upper-class and other speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris is the Egyptian deity of the dead and the underworld.

clue.text: Guest room rather awkward for baby carrier

indicators.note: awkward says these letters sit badly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A spare bedroom that is rather clumsy to use as a nursery for whoever carries the baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A surrogate mother bears a pregnancy for someone else, literally carrying their child in the womb.

clue.text: To sit down outside wood is most foolish

indicators.note: outside puts the resting word around the tree

parts.note: to sit down is to rest
ash is a tree and its timber

explanation.surface: Choosing to sit outdoors in the woods is the most foolish move.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash means reckless or hasty, so the superlative means acting with the least sense.

clue.text: What troubles me is adult being affected

indicators.note: the letters are troubled, that is disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the thing bothering them is being treated as a grown-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Affected manner is feigned or put on, just as simulated feeling is a pretence.

clue.text: Crossing the globe, exceedingly word-wise

indicators.note: the word for exceedingly stretches across and around the globe

parts.note: exceedingly means very
a globe is a ball

explanation.surface: A traveller going round the world and being extremely good with words.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbally means by means of words, so it describes things done in a word-based way.

clue.text: One corresponding offers two similar endorsements, one deficient

indicators.note: one of the pair falls short, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: a visa is an endorsement in a passport; two of them side by side

explanation.surface: A counterpart presents two matching passport stamps, one of them incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: Write VISA twice and drop the last A of the second to get VIS-A-VIS.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a vis-a-vis is a counterpart, someone in an equivalent position to another.

clue.text: Stir created by retreats with slight confusion at the end

indicators.note: only the last two letters get muddled, which here swaps them round

parts.note: routs are disorderly retreats

explanation.surface: A disturbance caused by soldiers falling back, ending in a little chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the final two letters of ROUTS: TS becomes ST.
explanation.definitionFit: To roust is to rouse or stir someone out, as from bed.

clue.text: Worm is found at foot of a cliff

indicators.note: in a down answer, the second piece sits below, at the foot of, the first

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff face

explanation.surface: A worm turns up lying at the bottom of a cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascaris is the genus of parasitic roundworms found in the intestines.

clue.text: What could become a son's lavish feed?

definitions.text: What could become a son's lavish feed?

indicators.note: the fodder letters could be turned into something else by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Asking what might turn into a lavish meal for a son.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: the miracle meal fed the multitude, and Jesus is the Son of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gospel miracle of the loaves and fishes multiplied a little food into a feast for thousands.

clue.text: Takes liberties quietly and then gets back to business

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
resumes means starts again after a pause

explanation.surface: Someone overstepping the mark, softly, before returning to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To presume is to behave overconfidently or overstep one's place, assuming permission.

clue.text: Open up, as you might say, an old letter

indicators.note: this flags that the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: to unseal is to open up something closed

explanation.surface: Breaking the seal on an ancient piece of correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'letter' is a missive; it is really a letter of the alphabet in an old script.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncial is a rounded capital script used in early medieval manuscripts, and one of its characters.

clue.text: Snow? All right to seek shelter in church

indicators.note: the okay letters take cover inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Is it fine to take refuge in a church during a snowfall?
explanation.walkthrough: Snow is slang for cocaine, not weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow and coke are both slang names for the drug cocaine, a white powder.

clue.text: What's spewed out by politicians, ladies and gentlemen?

parts.note: lava is what a volcano spews out
Tories are British Conservative politicians

explanation.surface: A jibe that politicians, addressed as ladies and gentlemen, spout rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Ladies and Gentlemen are the signs on toilet doors, so the phrase means toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies and Gents are British names for public toilets, so together they are lavatories.

clue.text: Over and done with computers etc — too old

parts.note: something over and done with is past
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: Someone finished with technology because they feel too old for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Past it is an idiom for no longer capable because of age.

clue.text: Promoter travels by ship, it's said, to island

indicators.note: this signals a word heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a ship sails
Man is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A publicist voyages by boat to an island, reportedly.
explanation.definitionFit: A salesman promotes and sells products on behalf of a company.

clue.text: Absurd English not to be found in our clues, I'd fancy

indicators.note: the English letter is absent from the letters that are rearranged
fancy as an anagram signal: the letters are given a fanciful new order

explanation.surface: The setter jokes that plain English is nowhere in these puzzles, which are silly.
explanation.walkthrough: OUR CLUES I'D minus E leaves OURCLUSID, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludicrous and absurd are synonyms for something so foolish it is laughable.

clue.text: Viewer more adventurous — what's being screened?

indicators.note: screened means hidden behind, so the query word is enclosed

parts.note: bolder means more daring
eh? is an exclamation meaning what?

explanation.surface: A cinema-goer who is more daring asks what film is showing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screened' suggests cinema, but here it means concealed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A beholder is one who looks at something, an onlooker.

clue.text: Quantity of works with no date

parts.note: opera is the plural of opus, a work

explanation.surface: A collection of compositions supplied without any date.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics an operand is the quantity on which an operation is performed.

clue.text: Viewer's screen's made of metal with authentic coating

indicators.note: the authentic word coats the metal, lying round it

parts.note: real means authentic
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: A display screen built from metal with a genuine outer layer.
explanation.walkthrough: The viewer is the eye; its screen is the retina, so the adjective means of the retina.
explanation.definitionFit: Retinal is the adjective for the retina, the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye.

clue.text: Old-fashioned US politician with something lyrical

parts.note: Dem is short for an American Democrat
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: An outdated American politician delivering a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Demode is a French borrowing meaning out of fashion.

clue.text: Sentimental mum with desire to restrict kid, initially

parts.note: ma is mother

indicators.note: the desire word holds the letter in, restricting it

parts.note: a wish is a desire

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of kid

explanation.surface: A soppy mother who wants to keep her child close.
explanation.definitionFit: Mawkish means sickly or excessively sentimental.

clue.text: Inflexible, as Stalin once could be

indicators.note: the letters could be reshaped into another word

explanation.surface: Stalin, an unbending dictator, could once be described as rigid.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonelastic describes material without stretch, so it cannot bend or flex.

clue.text: Past attempt to one's heart's desire

parts.note: ago means in the past
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: A former try at getting everything one wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A gogo is an idiom for in abundance, as much as one could want.

clue.text: Wife badly affected, just a bit

parts.note: to be hit is to be badly affected

explanation.surface: A wife who was hurt, but only slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: A whit is a tiny amount, the least particle.

clue.text: Conservative lot with love for something inexpensive

parts.note: a heap is a lot
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A Tory crowd who would gladly swap romance for a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapo is informal for a cheap item or a low-cost thing.

clue.text: Bits of stone troubling the lions

indicators.note: troubling disturbs the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Pebbles that pester the big cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoliths are stone tools or artefacts from the late Stone Age.

clue.text: Dark liquid that could be cloudier

indicators.note: the following word could be turned into another by reordering

explanation.surface: A murky fluid that might become even murkier.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrefined petroleum is a thick black fluid pumped from the ground.

clue.text: Rock is first thing for teenagers after school

indicators.note: the school letters come before the rest, which follows after
takes the opening letter of teenagers

explanation.surface: Rock music being the top priority for teenagers once lessons end.
explanation.definitionFit: Schist is a metamorphic rock that splits into thin layers.
